$summary: The raw hue ramps and the data-visualization palette. Everything except color.data.* is a reference target for the theme, never used directly in a component.

color.summary: Raw hue ramps, 50 → 950. `color.accent.*` and `color.neutral.*` are both generated from the theme's seed, so they re-tone per brand; the status hues are stated outright and do not. Every ramp is identical in light and dark — do not use any of them directly in a component.
use: Only as a reference target inside a theme's `tokens` map (packages/tokens/src/themes/*.mjs).
dont: Direct use in components — a ramp step is the same value in both schemes, so a component using one is unreadable in one of them.
Treating color.accent.* or color.neutral.* as a fixed palette — both follow the theme's seed, so their values depend on which theme is applied.

instead.Role fill, text, or tint: theme.accent-role.bg, theme.success-role.bg, theme.warning-role.bg, or theme.danger-role.bg (and each role's .fg / .subtle)

notes: Tonal ranges, for orientation only — these are not token names: 50-100 backgrounds (light), 200-300 borders (light), 400-500 low-emphasis text, 600-700 role fills and secondary text (light) / borders (dark), 800-950 primary text (light) / backgrounds and role subtles (dark).
color.accent.* is generated by expandColorScale from the seed's hue, with the ramp's tone, chroma and hue-drift curve held fixed — step 600 is the seed itself.

color.neutral.* is generated the same way, and its chroma additionally scales with neutralStyle, so the raw greys and the semantic greys in theme.bg.* come from one decision and cannot disagree about how grey the brand is. Fed its source ramp's own hue at cool chroma, the curve reproduces all eleven steps exactly.

A theme that states no accent still re-tones both ramps, from the default hue — the same thing the semantic neutrals already do. The ramps declared in src/primitives/color.json are the floor beneath that.

color.data.summary: Data-visualization palette — a categorical set for series identity, plus five-step sequential ramps per hue. The one palette group meant for direct use.
use: Chart series colors: color.data.categorical.* for discrete series, in the listed order, cycling if you run out.
A single-hue sequential ramp (color.data.blue, .teal, .orange, …) for a magnitude scale within one series.
color.data.neutral for a de-emphasized or 'other' series.
dont: UI chrome — buttons, backgrounds, text, borders. Use theme.* for all of that.
Assigning meaning by index alone across unrelated charts — keep a series-to-color mapping consistent within one view.
notes: Unlike every other palette group, these values are picked directly, not routed through a theme role — a chart's legend is not the same design problem as a button's background.
